rationale.intervention_reconstruction: The hypothesis proposes a composition change (equimolar WTaTiVZr vs. pure W) processed identically, while the paper used an as-cast arc-melted HEA versus commercially sintered pure W, so the processing route and baseline differ.
rationale.condition_agreement: The hypothesis specifies high-temperature tensile and fracture toughness at 900–1200 °C, whereas the paper used room-temperature compression, indentation plastometry up to 500 °C, and room-temperature scratch testing; the temperature regimes and test types are different.
rationale.mechanism_agreement: The hypothesis invokes lattice distortion lowering the Peierls barrier and enhancing dislocation mobility at high temperature, while the paper attributes improved plasticity to Ti, V, Zr effects (reduced valence-electron concentration, dislocation-core modification, grain-boundary cohesion) and does not isolate lattice distortion as the primary cause.
rationale.outcome_agreement: Both predict increased plastic strain and toughness relative to pure tungsten, but the hypothesis focuses on high-temperature ductility and a lower brittle-to-ductile transition, whereas the paper reports room-temperature plasticity, indentation cracking suppression above 200 °C, and scratch-based toughness improvement.
